note: Daily improvement ledger. Every entry must name an improvement and the pain it removes — recording activity alone is not a day.

entries.improvement: Sentinel CI goes green on every PR again, and the intrusive-tool parsers plus the authorization gate are hardened against hostile input.
entries.pain: CI Lint was red on every branch after the Go 1.26 rollover, and the security-critical parsers and scope matcher had no adversarial tests — a refactor could have silently opened a scope bypass.

entries.improvement: Spotter turns 'look at a device I own' into an honest identity, real-exposure risk, and a plain-language fix list — and RORY now runs as an always-on daemon that greets me with the brief and can power on Node 001 by voice.
entries.pain: There was no way to point at a camera and know if it was safe, and no hands-free 'Hey Jarvis' on the PC with the day's brief already prepared — every session started cold.

entries.improvement: Spotter's answer now reaches the Ray-Ban Display: a web-app bridge on Node 001 serves a glanceable HUD and runs the REAL `sentinel spot` on what the glass sees, and the Node 001 data plane it runs behind is written and validated — so the glasses and the desktop show the same audited answer from the same binary.
entries.pain: Spotter and RORY could only be reached from a terminal or a local page; there was no path onto the actual glasses and no server for them to talk to, so 'look at this device' was still a desk task, not a glance.
